title: Inside DC’s Power Struggle: James Gunn, Peter Safran Ousted After Tense Exec Clash and David Ellison’s Visit
body:
Warner Bros. Discovery’s newly‑formed DC Studios, led by James Gunn and Peter Safran, found their confidence shaken after an unexpected visit from Skydance co‑chiefs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz on the lot. The meeting, intended to smooth the transition after the Warner‑Skydance merger, instead highlighted deepening friction over creative control, budget authority and the future of the franchise’s flagship titles, including a planned third “Superman” film that had already entered early development.

When Gunn and Safran were tapped to helm the revitalized DC universe in early 2023, they were granted unprecedented leeway: a multi‑year, multi‑billion‑dollar slate, autonomy over casting and storytelling, and a promise that the studio would be insulated from the corporate turbulence that had plagued Warner Bros. in recent years. Their initial months were marked by rapid green‑lights for projects such as “The Authority,” “Blue Beetle,” and a sequel to “The Flash.” Behind the scenes, however, the duo was already negotiating the delicate balance between artistic ambition and the fiscal prudence demanded by a conglomerate still reeling from a costly merger.

The arrival of Skydance executives on a brisk Tuesday afternoon signaled a shift. Ellison, whose own production company has built a reputation for high‑concept, big‑budget spectacles, arrived with a clear agenda: to assess the viability of DC’s upcoming slate and to assert Skydance’s strategic priorities. Kreiz, formerly the head of Discovery’s streaming division, emphasized the need for tighter integration of the franchise’s content across theatrical releases, streaming platforms and merchandising pipelines. According to insiders, the discussion quickly turned from a courtesy briefing to a pointed interrogation of budgets, timelines and creative direction.

Gunn, known for his collaborative, writer‑friendly approach, reportedly pushed back against proposals to scale back the third “Superman” film’s budget, arguing that the character’s resurgence required a cinematic event on par with Marvel’s recent offerings. Safran, whose background in production management has kept the studio’s operations on schedule, expressed concerns that any abrupt changes could jeopardize already‑signed talent contracts and disrupt the momentum built with the franchise’s fanbase. The tension was palpable, and sources say the meeting concluded without a definitive resolution, leaving both sides to return to their offices with lingering doubts.

Industry analysts view the encounter as a microcosm of the larger challenges facing the newly merged Warner‑Skydance entity. The merger was billed as a means to combine Warner Bros.’ storied intellectual property with Skydance’s production expertise and capital, but the integration has revealed divergent corporate cultures. While Skydance executives are accustomed to a top‑down decision‑making model that emphasizes blockbuster profitability, Gunn and Safran have championed a more decentralized, creator‑driven process that seeks to rebuild trust with a skeptical audience after a string of missteps in the DC film line.

The fallout could have tangible repercussions for the franchise’s release schedule. The third “Superman” film, tentatively titled “Superman: Legacy,” was slated for a summer 2027 debut, with pre‑production already underway. If budgetary constraints are imposed, the project may face delays or a re‑imagining that could dilute its intended scope. Moreover, the broader DC slate—encompassing sequels, spin‑offs and television series—may undergo a strategic audit, potentially reshuffling release windows to better align with Skydance’s cross‑platform distribution goals.

Looking ahead, the next few months will be critical in determining whether Gunn and Safran can retain their creative helm or whether Skydance will assert greater oversight. Both parties have expressed a public commitment to “collaboration” and “shared vision,” but the underlying power dynamics suggest a negotiation still in flux. As the studio navigates this internal crossroads, fans and investors alike will be watching closely to see if the partnership can deliver a cohesive, high‑quality DC universe or if the friction will lead to a recalibration of leadership and strategy. The outcome will shape not only the fate of Superman’s next chapter but also the broader trajectory of one of Hollywood’s most ambitious franchise overhauls.
